rv.q: The long grass blows and the sky, thanks to Jack Knowles’ emotive lighting, seems to throb with the promise of other, grander lives playing out somewhere far away. It might have felt a bit static were it not for Pickett’s brilliant eye for detail and three captivating central performances.

Much of the energy of Lyndsey Turner’s artfully stylised, superbly performed production comes from the back-and-forth banter between these three women, whose scythe-like wit and anachronistic irreverence dazzle like rain in the sun.
The representation of what it is like to move as a woman in a patriarchal society – whether in 1536 or 2025 – was absolutely brilliant.
This is an original and exciting debut, given an exceptional production by director Lyndsey Turner and an outstanding cast.
